title: Amazon Neptune
summary: An example of querying RDF data through SPARQL in a managed graph database.

sections.label: Documented role
sections.text: Amazon Neptune documents SPARQL access to RDF data. Engine-specific behavior must be checked against its compliance documentation.

sections.label: What Atlas provides
sections.text: Selecting Neptune includes the existing RDF and SPARQL review questions. These do not configure database access or verify engine-specific behavior.

sections.label: Check in your environment
sections.text: Confirm the actual version, supported interface, permissions, data model and expected query results. Compare alternatives using your constraints.

sections.label: Gap review: workflow use and checks
items: Recommended workflow use: Architecture and impact, Development, Tests and review. Use for an affected Neptune RDF interface when choosing the query boundary, implementing that boundary and verifying engine-specific results. This is an Atlas recommendation reviewed on 2026-10-15, not a mandatory process or an observed execution result.
Check output to obtain: Record the actual engine version, approved endpoint, caller scope and intended graph dataset in the interface decision.
Check output to obtain: Compare a permitted fixture and a named-graph boundary fixture with their expected bindings using the application identity.
Check output to obtain: Preserve observed query output and any blocked permission or environment check separately from planned expectations.

confidence: Documented facts have scoped sources. Suitability for a particular project remains unverified.

catalog.applicability: Use this technology example when your data is RDF and you query it with SPARQL in a managed graph database. Confirm the actual version, supported interface, permissions and engine specific behavior before relying on it.
catalog.limits: Catalogue inclusion is not a recommendation, configured access or verified compatibility.
